section.label: Phiogy for Windows
section.lead: The Windows app: getting it, what it needs, where it connects.

article.title: Get the app
article.lead: Phiogy for Windows is a folder you keep, not an installer. Its download opens again soon.
step: Download phiogy-windows.zip from the Download page once it opens.
Unzip it where you like: the Phiogy folder holds phiogy.exe, README.txt and the asset folder.
Keep the asset folder beside phiogy.exe.
Open phiogy.exe and sign in with your Phiace account.

article.title: What it needs
article.lead: Windows 10 or 11 and a graphics card with DirectX 11.
step: The first start can take half a minute while Windows checks the new program; later starts are quick.
Calls use the microphone and camera only while you are in a call.

article.title: Where it connects
article.lead: The app meets the same server as phiegg.com: your hosts, rooms and calls are the same in the app and in the browser.
step: Accounts and data: phiegg.com/api.
Calls: phiegg.com/wrt.
Pictures and downloads: phiegg.com/cdn.

section.label: Phiogy in your browser
section.lead: Rooms, calls, hosts and friends with nothing to download.

article.title: Open Phiogy in your browser
article.lead: Rooms, calls, hosts and friends run in the browser; a few things, such as Work sync, are only in the Windows app.
step: Go to phiogy.com and press Open Phiogy.
Sign in, or make an account: one account opens every Phi app.

article.title: On a Mac
article.lead: There is no Mac app yet.
step: Open Phiogy in your browser: your hosts, rooms and calls are the same there.

section.label: For the team
section.lead: What Work sync does on your machine, and what it never takes.

article.title: What Work sync does
article.lead: Work sync copies the files your team needs from your machine to your team's server.
step: Once you sign in on Phiogy for Windows, your machine joins your team's server. No code is needed.
Nothing is copied until an administrator connects your machine.
After that, only the files an administrator picks are copied.
The Work sync drawer in Phiogy shows what it is doing.

article.title: What it never takes
article.lead: Only the folders your administrator chose are looked at: Documents, Downloads and Videos to begin with.
step: Files over 200 MB are left out.
Until a file is picked, the server sees only its name, size and dates.

section.label: For administrators
section.lead: Connect machines, pick files, pause or take one off.

article.title: Connect a machine
article.lead: Pressing Connect is your consent, given once; from then on the machine syncs by itself.
step: Sign in on phiegg.com as an administrator and open phiegg.com/work.
Find the machine by its person and name.
Press Connect, then Sync now.

article.title: Pick the files
article.lead: Only the files you tick are copied to the server.
step: Press Open on a machine.
Under On this machine, newest first, tick the files to copy.
Press Sync selected. Each file shows under Files, with a Download link, once it is on the server.

article.title: Invite someone first
article.lead: A person you name beforehand joins already connected.
step: Under Invite a machine, write their handle or email and press Invite.
When they sign in on Phiogy for Windows, their machine joins and starts syncing.

article.title: Pause or take a machine off
article.lead: Only administrators start, pause or end a machine's sync.
step: Press Pause to stop taking files, and Resume to start again.
Press Take off to end the machine's access: its key stops working.

section.label: The server
section.lead: Phiora: the one server under every Phi app.

article.title: Phiora
article.lead: Phiogy, Phiegg and the other Phi apps share one server, Phiora, at phiegg.com/api.
step: Accounts are shared: one sign-in for every app.
An app's menus and pages come from Phiora, or from the app's own data file when Phiora has none.

article.title: The work machines API
article.lead: How a machine and the administrators talk to Phiora about Work sync.
step: POST /machine/consent: a signed-in person's machine joins.
POST /machine/beat: the machine says it is there and hears its folders.
POST /machine/index: the machine lists its files; the server answers with the ones it wants.
PUT /machine/file: the machine sends one file.
GET /machine and GET /machine/<id>/listing: what administrators read; POST /machine/<id>/pick chooses the files.

section.label: Sites as data
section.lead: A site is one data file of pages and blocks.

article.title: A site is a data file
article.lead: phiogy.com is one JSON file: its pages, each a list of blocks, with a top bar and a footer round every page.
step: Blocks are the kit's: bar, hero, marquee, grid, help, prose, news, faq and footer.
A link names a page of the site (view), another app (app) or an address (href); off shows it without leading anywhere.
These docs are a help block reading their own file.

section.label: Calls
section.lead: How a call is set up.

article.title: How calls run
article.lead: Calls go between the people in them over WebRTC, met through the line at phiegg.com/wrt.
step: Up to 8 people with camera, microphone and screen.
The microphone and camera are used only while you are in a call.
